patch.value: pm update --unset blocked_by (or --blocked-by none) deletes every blocked_by edge, not only the scalar's: clearing blocker A silently drops an independent prerequisite B

Reproduced on the feat/write-time-preconditions build (2026.11.2 source). An item with scalar blocked_by=A plus blocked_by edges to A and to an independent prerequisite B: pm update <id> --unset blocked_by leaves blocked_by unset and the dependency list EMPTY. Cause: applyBlockedByMutation clears the scalar and calls reconcileBlockedByDependency(current, undefined), which filters out every kind=blocked_by dependency. The edge to B was never the scalar's. The item then reads as unblocked: next selects it, start admission admits it, and validate no longer flags it, while B is still open. No warning names the dropped edges. Found by the Codex review of PR 1654: pm-urzubi's start refusal had advertised --unset blocked_by as its recovery command; that refusal now advertises it only when the scalar's blocker is the item's only blocked_by edge. Related: pm-scbr0s (the close-time blocker-clear warning names one of N deleted ordering edges) and pm-q6gx (--blocked-by overwrite).

Clearing the blocked_by scalar removes at most the edge(s) that point at the scalar's own target, never an independent blocked_by edge; Removing every blocked_by edge requires an explicit, separately named operation (or --clear-deps-like flag) whose receipt lists the removed edges; Regression test: scalar A with edges A and B, unset scalar, B remains and the item stays blocked; The start_blocked_by_open_dependency recovery may then advertise the scalar clear again for multi-edge items
pm update <id> --unset blocked_by clears the scalar and its own edge, keeping independent blocked_by prerequisites
All blocked_by edges are removed: dependencies goes from [B:blocked_by, A:blocked_by] to [] after --unset blocked_by

value.text: Scope evidence from the Codex review round 3 of PR 1654: dependency removal cannot address legacy blocker rows either. --dep-remove normalizes its selector id through normalizeItemReference and compares kinds literally. So a row stored with a short id (missing, normalized to pm-missing), an alias kind (depends_on, which canonicalizes to blocked_by everywhere else) or an external locator without source_kind in the selector (gh:org/repo#12, normalized to pm-gh:org/repo#12) fails with dependency_remove_no_match. Combined with this item's --unset blocked_by data loss, some blockers have no safe single-command removal. pm-urzubi's refusal therefore offers 'pm get <id> --fields blocked_by,dependencies' for them. Fixing this item should make removal selectors canonical (id normalization plus resolveCanonicalRelationshipKind) so recovery can advertise an executable removal again.
